audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Skill, Singed, Singed, Skill, Skill, Singed, Singed on both layers.
audit.why: audits/top/aurora__singed.json set her side to Singed, Singed, Singed, Aurora, Aurora, Skill, Singed, and the singed packet levelChart says exactly the same thing. Levels 4-6 really are her window — Twofold Hex out-ranges everything Singed owns and Across the Veil answers the first Fling.
audit.corrected: win[0] and phases[0].side to Singed; win[3]/win[4] and phases[3]/[4].side to Aurora; win[5] and phases[5].side to Skill. Proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: The tracked cooldown is an ability that does not exist, and no number appears anywhere.
audit.why: Across the Veil is 22s at rank 1 — the longest ability cooldown in her kit and the one you must bait. Twofold Hex is 9s, The Weirding 15s, Between Worlds 140s. Against Singed's 17s adhesive and 10s Fling, only the 22s leap is a real window.
audit.corrected: 22s Across the Veil, 9s Twofold Hex and 140s Between Worlds written into the cooldown row, spikes, whys and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fabrications, all load-bearing. (a) 'Twofold Hunt' is not an ability — Riot's Q is Twofold Hex, and the name appears 25 times across the full layer as the thing to track. (b) 'root-on-return' and 'Twofold Hunt root' — Aurora has no root anywhere in her kit; Twofold Hex curses and drags, The Weirding slows. (c) 'Spirit Refuge' and 'Icy ground' are not Aurora abilities at all. (d) Between Worlds (R, 140s) is treated as her level-2 escape; her escape is Across the Veil (W, 22s). And the one interaction that decides the lane is missing: Mega Adhesive GROUNDS, and both Across the Veil and Between Worlds are dashes, so glued she cannot leap at all.
audit.why: Riot text — Aurora Q: 'sends out a missile that curses any enemies it hits... recast to draw active curses back toward herself'. W: 'leaps in a direction... becoming invisible'. E: 'damages and slows enemies before Aurora hops backward'. R: 'leaps... creates an area that slows enemies within it'. Singed W: 'slowing and grounding enemies who walk on it'. The same fabrications were found from her side in audits/top/aurora__singed.json.
audit.corrected: Real names throughout, the grounding of both her leaps stated, the fake root replaced with the real Fling-into-adhesive root, and Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds against Spirit Abjuration's healing added.

audit.why: Her passive spawns spirits off everything she damages and they heal her — that is what carries her through a poison-chip lane, and Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds is the direct answer.

edits.before: At level 1 Aurora out-ranges you and her Twofold Hunt poke is free — do not run at her or you hand her the lane. Last-hit on the outer edge of Poison Trail, absorb the small poke, and let your passive movement speed make up the drift. At level 2 Fling comes online and changes the math: she has no escape yet, so any time she steps inside your personal space to Q you, punish immediately — Fling her into your cloud and disengage before she can root you on the Twofold Hunt return. By level 3 your full root-Fling combo can oneshot her health bar if Between Worlds is on cooldown; once you confirm it is down, walk up, drop Mega Adhesive in her retreat path, Fling her into it, and let the cloud do its work.
edits.after: At level 1 Aurora out-ranges you and Twofold Hex (9s) is free poke — do not run at her or you hand her the lane. Last-hit on the outer edge of Poison Trail, absorb the chip, and let your passive move speed make up the drift. At level 2 Fling changes the math: she has no leap yet, so the moment she steps inside your space to Q, punish — Fling her into your cloud and disengage before the recast drags the curse back through you. By level 3 the real combo is live, and it is not a root you throw: Mega Adhesive GROUNDS, so glue her retreat path and Across the Veil will not cast at all, then Fling her into the goo — landing in the adhesive is what roots her, and the cloud does the rest.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are Aurora's best window — her Twofold Hunt root range forces you to respect every step forward and her Between Worlds gives her an instant escape the moment you commit. The correct answer is to proxy the wave behind her tower or farm the triangle: deny her the comfortable poke lane she needs to snowball, and bank gold without standing in her kill zone. At level 6, Insanity Potion gives you the speed and tankiness to re-engage through Spirit Refuge — run past the spirit form, stay on her, and let the poison cloud tick while she burns cooldowns trying to create distance. She cannot permanently blink away from a Rylai's-slowed Singed who ults and ghosts simultaneously.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are Aurora's best window — Twofold Hex out-ranges every step you take and Across the Veil (22s) answers your first commit. The correct play is to proxy behind her tower or farm the triangle: deny her the comfortable poke lane and bank gold without standing in her kill zone. At level 6 Insanity Potion (100s) does two things — the stats let you re-engage through The Weirding's slow, and the Grievous Wounds it puts on Poison Trail halves the Spirit Abjuration healing she leans on. Stay on her and let the cloud tick while she burns the 22s leap. She cannot keep leaping away from a Rylai's-slowed Singed who is ulted and ghosted at the same time.

notes: Four fabrications removed: the ability name 'Twofold Hunt' (Q is Twofold Hex), a root Aurora does not have, the non-existent 'Spirit Refuge' and 'Icy ground', and the treatment of Between Worlds (R, 140s) as her level-2 escape when her escape is Across the Veil (W, 22s). audits/top/aurora__singed.json found the same root fabrication from her side and suggests a repo-wide grep for 'root' in champ-data/content/aurora.js. The decisive interaction — Mega Adhesive grounds and both her leaps are dashes — was absent from both layers. Level chart flipped to match that mirror and the packet, which agree with each other.
